messages:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty triggered (INC-102348) 2025-11-19T07:12:08Z — Incident: high SRV/DNS failures reported from AZ-B. Paging: @net-oncall, @alex, @mira.
net-oncall: ack — I'm on it. Starting telemetry checks for AZ-B egress and peering.
alex: seeing lots of SRV lookup timeouts and SERVFAILs from app traces in AZ-B. Early numbers: ~15% SRV failure rate for internal lookups, some downstream 502s from product API. Snippet from coredns logs:
```
Nov 19 07:10:55 coredns[1]: plugin/forward: read udp 10.4.3.2:51234->172.25.8.10:53: i/o timeout
Nov 19 07:11:03 kube-proxy: srv lookup error: lookup _grpc._tcp.service.namespace.svc.cluster.local: SERVFAIL
```
mira: Consul control plane in AZ-B shows increased RPC latency and transient leader elections. Etcd proxied connections see retransmits. Also noticing interface tx drops on the AZ egress gateway.
net-oncall: running `ethtool -S eth0 | grep tx_errors` and `tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` on a couple of edge NATs — sustained tx_errors and qdisc drops on egress queue. Cloud provider event stream shows a "transit fabric congestion" warning for AZ-B around 07:08.
jen: raising customer-impact channel and paging support ops. Which customers/regions are hit?
alex: mostly US-west traffic routed to AZ-B. We're seeing elevated error rates for a handful of customer clusters and internal backend APIs. Marking pages P1 for impacted customers. Posting initial status:.
ops-mgr: acknowledged. Please capture timeline. We'll notify customers in affected orgs once mitigation is known.
sam: mitigation suggestion: two-step approach — short term: route DNS/TCP lookups to regional TCP-forwarding resolvers (they tolerate UDP drops better), or enable DNS-over-TCP fallback in coredns; longer term: ask cloud for fabric remediation. Can we try enabling TCP forwarding in CoreDNS and a canary DNS cache on nodes?
net-oncall: agree with canary. I'm hesitant to change all forwarders immediately. Propose: stand up a lightweight dnsmasq cache on a subset of nodes that forwards to AZ-A resolvers over TCP and point a canary namespace to it. If that works, we can update core config. Also opening a firewall rule to allow TCP/UDP 53 to az-a resolvers.
alex: preparing canary. Commands:
```
# deploy dnsmasq as a DaemonSet in az-b-canary ns, forward to az-a resolvers via TCP
kubectl -n az-b-canary apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: dns-cache
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: dnsmasq
        image: busybox
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/usr/sbin/dnsmasq --no-daemon --server=10.200.1.21#53 --server=10.200.1.22#53 --port=53"]
EOF
kubectl -n az-b-canary patch configmap coredns --patch '{"data":{"Corefile":".:53 {\n    forward . 127.0.0.1\n}\n"}}' --context=az-b-canary
kubectl -n az-b-canary rollout restart deployment/coredns --context=az-b-canary
```
deploy-bot: dns-cache DaemonSet created in az-b-canary (deploy id d-7902). CoreDNS patch applied to canary namespace.
net-oncall: firewall/routes opened to az-a resolvers for TCP/UDP 53. Monitoring packet drops.
alex: canary shows SRV failures drop to <1% for pods using dnsmasq within 60s. P95 lookup latency increased ~60ms (cross-AZ), but success rate recovered.
jen: posting status update: "Mitigation in progress — using regional DNS failover to restore service discovery for affected AZ-B workloads." Expect another update in 10m.
mira: preliminary root cause hypothesis: egress fabric in AZ-B is dropping a subset of small UDP packets (likely checksum/MTU/bufferly issue) causing DNS/CONSUL heartbeats to fail; TCP is less affected. We'll include packet captures and provider ticket.
sam: recommendation: enable CoreDNS to prefer TCP for upstream lookups (forward plugin supports `prefer_tcp`) and add local caching. Can we roll prefer_tcp in a staggered rollout?
net-oncall: yep. Plan: roll `prefer_tcp` in core config for kube-system coredns, staggered by AZ-B node groups (10% at a time). Also create automatic fallback rule in platform runbooks: if SRV failure rate > 5% for 5m, switch CoreDNS to prefer TCP and add dns cache. Filing infra follow-up ticket INF-4022 for provider engagement.
alex: executing staged rollout: patch applied to one replica set, rollout id r-5520 initiated.
deploy-bot: rollout started for kube-system/coredns in context az-b (rollout id r-5520).
net-oncall: monitoring. SRV failures fall from 15% -> 1.2% over 2 minutes as additional replicas flip. Latency p95 up ~70-90ms.
ops-mgr: customers showing recovery. Updating status page to "service degraded (mitigated)" and emailing impacted contacts.
mira: collecting logs/pcaps and uploading to infra bucket for postmortem. Noted consul elections correlated with peak drops; we'll include those traces.
jen: scheduling postmortem in 48 hours. Please add any important artifacts to the incident doc.
alex: include rollout id r-5520 and dns-cache deploy id d-7902 in timeline. Also note exact config diff and timestamps.
sam: ops follow-up rec: consider TCP-first resolvers for control-plane traffic and increase egress queue sizing in AZ-B until provider fix. Also consider health-based automatic fallback to cross-AZ resolvers.
net-oncall: provider ticket created INF-4022 with cloud vendor, reference: egress fabric alerts and pcap. Workaround remains active — prefer_tcp + caching — until provider confirms fix.
jen: marking incident as Mitigated on status page. Closing active page; handing over to infrastructure runbook owners and infra ticketing for long-term fix. Any final notes? :eyes:
ops-mgr: include a short customer-facing summary and timeline. Good job.
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-102348 status updated to 'mitigated' at 2025-11-19T07:23:22Z — responders: net-oncall, alex, mira, sam, jen, ops-mgr
